pinterest.title: Wedding Place Cards Ideas for Every Table, from Calligraphy to Acrylic
pinterest.description: Wedding place cards ideas grouped by style so you can shortlist quickly: classic paper and calligraphy, natural and edible, keepsakes that double as favours, glass and acrylic, local touches and cards that sit on the napkin or plate. Plus how to keep every name readable by candlelight and check spelling and preferred names against your seating plan.

pinterest.title: Natural and Edible Wedding Place Cards: Leaves, Herbs, Fruit and Biscuits
pinterest.description: Natural wedding place card ideas for a garden or summer table: a magnolia or olive leaf lettered in gold or white ink, a rosemary ring tied around the napkin, a lemon or fig with a small tag, or a biscuit iced with a name. Letter leaves close to the day, keep them cool, and give your caterer the ingredients of every edible card and the list of guests with allergies.

pinterest.title: Glass, Mirror and Acrylic Wedding Place Cards That Catch the Candlelight
pinterest.description: Clear and reflective wedding name cards suit a rooftop or city ballroom: laser cut acrylic names on the plate or glass rim, mirror tiles with white or gold lettering, or names applied to each wine glass. Choose a tinted or frosted finish so the name reads against white linen, and check with your venue before lettering its glassware.

slides: Wedding place cards: the smallest piece of stationery, and the one every guest picks up.
Classic paper. Calligraphy on a folded card, a painted tile that stays put in a breeze, or a bookmark laid across the plate.
Natural and edible. A magnolia or olive leaf, a rosemary ring around the napkin, a lemon with a tag, or a biscuit iced with a name.
Keepsakes that double as favours. A named glass, a slice of agate, a slate heart or a small plant in a tiny pot.
Glass, mirror and acrylic. Choose a tinted or frosted finish, or contrasting lettering, so the name reads against white linen.
Readable after dark. Strong contrast, the same spot on every setting, and little else on the card. Test a sample by candlelight.
One source for every name: your finished seating plan. Check titles, preferred names and every surname before anything is made.
Marrying overseas? Make the cards at home and carry them, or make them near the venue? Ask us: a Wedded Advisor can talk it through with you.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Place cards are a small detail, and every guest picks one up. We have grouped our wedding place cards ideas by style so you can shortlist in a minute: classic paper, natural and edible, keepsakes, glass and acrylic, local touches, and cards that rest on the napkin or plate.

A few things to settle before you choose:
Take every name from your finished seating plan, and check spelling, titles and preferred names.
Edible cards are food, so give your caterer the list of what is in them and of guests with allergies.
On a terrace, paper flies. Weight cards with a holder, tie them to the napkin, or choose tile, stone or glass.
For a wedding overseas, decide early who sets the cards out on the day.

Which style suits your table? Tell us in the comments, or start a conversation with a Wedded Advisor through Wedded Concierge. The full guide is at the link in our bio.
